title: Three-dimensional coordinate systems
goal: Get comfortable plotting points $(x, y, z)$, planes, spheres, and distances in 3D space before we start doing calculus on 3D surfaces.

beforeThis.skill: 3D distance is just the 2D Pythagorean formula with $+ \Delta z^2$ tacked onto the end under the square root: $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2 + (z_2-z_1)^2}$.

seeIt.title: Functions of Two Variables & 3D Graphs
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Introduces visualizing points, coordinate planes, and surfaces in three-dimensional $(x, y, z)$ space.

questions.asking: Spot which shaded wall or floor in the 3D diagram is the $xy$-, $yz$-, and $xz$-plane, and match each corner of the dark triangle to its axis intercept.
questions.statement:
Part of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is sketched below, along with a triangle.

Identify the following parts of the sketch:

  1. the $xy$-plane
  2. the $yz$-plane
  3. the $xz$-plane
  4. the vertex of the triangle lying on $(1, 0, 0)$
  5. the vertex of the triangle lying on $(0, 1, 0)$
  6. the vertex of the triangle lying on $(0, 0, 1)$

figures.alt: First octant of R^3 with positive x-axis pointing down-left, positive y-axis pointing down-right, and positive z-axis pointing straight up. Three coordinate planes meet at the origin, and a dark shaded triangle connects one vertex on each positive coordinate axis.

questions.statement: What is the distance from the point $(1, 2, 3)$ to the point $(4, -5, 6)$?

questions.asking: Find the straight-line 3D distance from the nest after converting the north, east, and altitude displacements into consistent units.
questions.statement: A bird sets off from its nest. It flies one kilometre due north, then two kilometres due east, gaining $100$ metres of altitude. How far is it from its nest?
